newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage rates fell to three-month low.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage rates fell to three-month low.

text.p: Mortgage rates fell this week to the lowest levels in more than three months as bond market interest rates continued to fall on fresh signs of mild inflation, Freddie Mac said Thursday.

Fixed-rate mortgages fell for the second consecutive week. Thirty-year mortgages averaged 7.72 percent, the lowest since a rate of 7.65 percent in the week ended Feb. 28, 1997. Last week's 30-year rate averaged 7.85 percent.
Fifteen-year mortgages fell to 7.27 percent from 7.40 percent, the lowest since 7.15 percent in the Feb. 28 week.
One-year adjustable mortgage rates dipped to 5.67 percent from 5.78 percent last week, Freddie Mac said. The rate has not been lower since 5.61 percent in the week ended March 14.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 8.39 percent, the 15-year 7.90 percent and the adjustable loan 5.91 percent.
"Interest rates have slipped lower in the last two weeks on news of slower growth and very low inflation," Robert Van Order, Freddie Mac chief economist, said in a statement.

"Also, the markets seem confident the Federal Reserve will not raise rates in early July and this gives us the indication mortgage interest rates will not rise much, if at all, in at least the near future," Van Order added.
Freddie Mac is a corporation chartered by Congress that buys mortgages from lenders and packages them into securities for investors.
